title: An efficient protocol to use iron oxide nanoparticles in microfluidic paper device for arsenic detection
author: Chauhan, Upadhyay

steps.title: Clean injection vials
steps.instruction: Prepare piranha solution by mixing concentrated H₂SO₄ and H₂O₂ in a 3:1 volume ratio, wash the discarded injection vials with this solution, then autoclave the vials to remove contaminants.

steps.title: Prepare arsenic stock solution
steps.instruction: Mix 10 mg of As₂O₃ with 10 mL of lemon juice to obtain the standard arsenic stock solution used for all subsequent analyses.

steps.title: Synthesize iron oxide nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Produce bare and cysteine‑capped iron oxide nanoparticles using green tea extract as a reducing agent.

substeps.instruction: Mix green tea extract with 0.01 M FeCl₃ solution in a 1:1 (v/v) ratio; the reduction of Fe³⁺ to iron oxide is indicated by an immediate black coloration.
For cysteine‑capped nanoparticles, add 0.02 M L‑cysteine to the above mixture during synthesis to provide surface capping.

steps.title: Characterize nanoparticles by TEM and XRD
steps.instruction: Analyze the cysteine‑capped iron oxide nanoparticles by transmission electron microscopy to confirm spherical morphology and a size range of 20–50 nm, and by X‑ray diffraction to verify amorphous structure and high purity.

steps.title: Fabricate microfluidic paper device
steps.instruction: Create a μPAD on filter paper and impregnate it with silver nitrate for arsenic detection.

substeps.instruction: Cut filter paper into a circular disk of 1 cm diameter.
Draw a 0.5 cm × 0.5 cm square on each side of the disk using a Camlin permanent marker to form a hydrophobic zone.
Air‑dry the marked paper for 5 min.
Place the paper in a hot‑air oven at 70 °C for 1 h to evaporate the ink solvent and solidify the hydrophobic barrier.
Spot 20 µL of 5 % (w/v) AgNO₃ solution onto the hydrophobic detection zone.
Dry the spotted paper in darkness, then store it in an amber‑colored airtight zipper bag at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Detect arsenic using μPAD assay
steps.instruction: Perform the arsenic detection reaction inside injection vials and record the color change on the μPAD.

substeps.instruction: Secure the prepared μPAD to the inner surface of the rubber cap of a 10 mL injection vial using double‑sided tape (or to a screw‑cap with a PTFE septum).
Add 1 mL of the arsenic sample (or standard) to the vial.
Add 0.5 mL of the iron oxide nanoparticle solution (bare or cysteine‑capped) to generate arsine gas.
Lightly shake the vial to mix the contents.
Incubate the vial at room temperature for 10 min.
Observe the development of a reddish‑brown color on the μPAD, indicating formation of a silver‑arsine complex.
Remove the μPAD for image capture; run a parallel blank without nanoparticle addition for reference.

steps.title: Analyze color intensity with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Quantify the μPAD color response using ImageJ software.

substeps.instruction: Scan the reacted μPAD with a desktop scanner to obtain a digital image.
Open the image in ImageJ and convert it to RGB color mode.
Measure the mean intensity of the red channel for each sample and the blank; higher arsenic concentrations correspond to higher mean intensity values.
